description:
In repos/activity-api/src/routes/execution-traces.ts, change one query expression so that an equality filter combined with it is no longer silently dropped.

The file contains exactly one occurrence of this two-line fragment (the second line disambiguates it from a similar push elsewhere in the file):
      whereConditions.push('executed_at >= type::datetime($start_date)');
      params.start_date = startDate;

Replace it with exactly this:
      whereConditions.push('executed_at >= <datetime> $start_date');
      params.start_date = startDate;

One file, one op. The only change is type::datetime($start_date) becoming <datetime> $start_date inside the pushed string. Do not modify the params line, any other line, or any other file. The replacement contains no backslash characters.

WHY. When a WHERE clause combines an equality filter with a datetime bound written as type::datetime(parameter), the equality filter is silently dropped and the query returns every row in the time range. Reproduced against the live database on 2026-09-11 using the exact shape this route emits:

  org_id = 'organizations:substrate' AND executed_at >= type::datetime($start) returns 1153
  org_id = 'organizations:nonexistent_xyz' AND executed_at >= type::datetime($start) returns 1153
  no org filter at all, same bound, returns 1153

An organization that does not exist returns the full time range, so the org_id predicate has no effect. This route is the trace read path and it builds exactly this clause alongside an org_id equality filter.

The cast form fixes it, verified with a discriminating control rather than only a zero:

  org_id = 'organizations:substrate' AND executed_at >= <datetime> $start returns 970
  org_id = 'organizations:metabob' AND executed_at >= <datetime> $start returns 0, its rows being older than the window
  org_id = 'organizations:nonexistent_xyz' AND executed_at >= <datetime> $start returns 0
  no org filter, same bound, returns 1177

So the cast returns a real count for a real organization and zero for one that does not exist, which is the behaviour the plain form fails to produce.

WHY IT MATTERS. The execution table holds rows for more than one organization: organizations:substrate 46715, organizations:metabob 1675, and unknown 2395. This service connects to the database as root, and a root system user bypasses table PERMISSIONS, so the application-level org_id predicate is the only isolation control on this path. With the predicate inoperative, a trace read scoped to one organization can return another organization's rows.

The equivalent expression on the second push in this file, and the selected_at one further down, are separate edits and are deliberately not included here.
